task_summary: Define the interface contract for the 'Shared UI Components' module (id: shared_ui) in a TypeScript/React documentation website. This module owns four presentational components — CodeBlock, VersionBadge, YouTubeEmbed, CalloutBox — plus their prop types (CodeBlockProps, VersionBadgeProps, YouTubeEmbedProps, CalloutBoxProps) and the CalloutVariant enum. Must follow strict TypeScript, named exports only, `export type {}` for type aliases, and include vitest + @testing-library/react contract tests.

findings.finding: Best practice for presentational React components is to define props as a standalone exported type (using `export type { }`) and then use that type as the single generic parameter to `React.FC` or as a function parameter annotation. For shared_ui, each component's props interface is already defined in the canonical registry (CodeBlockProps, VersionBadgeProps, YouTubeEmbedProps, CalloutBoxProps). These must be exported as types via `export type { CodeBlockProps, ... }` and the components themselves as named runtime exports via `export { CodeBlock, ... }`. Avoid `React.FC` if you want to keep the contract minimal — prefer explicit function signatures with return type `React.ReactElement`.
findings.relevance: Directly governs how the four shared components are typed and exported

findings.topic: Enum vs Union Type for CalloutVariant
findings.finding: The canonical registry defines CalloutVariant as an enum with variants gotcha | warning | tip. In TypeScript, string literal union types (`type CalloutVariant = 'gotcha' | 'warning' | 'tip'`) are preferred over `enum` for serializable, tree-shakeable values — but the registry says 'enum'. The safest approach that satisfies both strict TS and the registry is a `const` enum or a plain string union exported via `export type`. Since the operating procedures say `export type { }` for type aliases, a string union type is the idiomatic choice: `export type CalloutVariant = 'gotcha' | 'warning' | 'tip';` — this still matches the registry's intent (fixed set of variants) while being fully compatible with JSON serialization and vi.mock rules.
findings.source: TypeScript handbook — Enums vs Union Types; project operating procedures
findings.relevance: CalloutVariant is owned by shared_ui and consumed by page_content; incorrect form would break cross-module contracts

findings.finding: CodeBlock uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. In vitest + jsdom, `navigator.clipboard` is undefined by default. The established pattern is to mock it in test setup: `Object.assign(navigator, { clipboard: { writeText: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined) } })`. Alternatively, use `vi.stubGlobal`. The copy handler should be async and handle errors gracefully (try/catch around writeText). Tests should verify: (1) clicking the copy button calls writeText with the exact `code` prop value, (2) the button provides feedback (e.g., text changes to 'Copied!'), (3) error state is handled if writeText rejects.
findings.relevance: CodeBlock's copy-to-clipboard is the most complex behavior in shared_ui and the most likely source of test failures

findings.finding: YouTubeEmbed should: (1) Use youtube-nocookie.com domain for privacy-enhanced embedding, (2) Extract video ID from various YouTube URL formats (watch?v=, youtu.be/, /embed/) using a parsing utility, (3) Set `sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin'` and `allow='accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture'` on the iframe, (4) Use `loading='lazy'` for performance, (5) Responsive pattern: wrap iframe in a container with `aspect-video` (Tailwind class) for 16:9 ratio. The URL-to-embed-URL conversion is a common pitfall — must handle edge cases like URLs with timestamps, playlists, and extra query params.
findings.source: YouTube IFrame API docs, OWASP iframe embedding guidelines, Tailwind CSS aspect-ratio plugin
findings.relevance: YouTubeEmbed is a shared component; incorrect URL parsing or missing security attributes would affect all pages with videos

findings.finding: A common pattern for variant-driven styling in Tailwind is a variant-to-classes lookup map: `const variantStyles: Record<CalloutVariant, string> = { gotcha: 'border-red-500 bg-red-50', warning: 'border-yellow-500 bg-yellow-50', tip: 'border-green-500 bg-green-50' }`. This is type-safe (exhaustive via Record), readable, and easy to test. Each variant should also include an icon/emoji and an aria-label or role='alert' (for warning) / role='note' (for tip/gotcha) for accessibility.
findings.source: Tailwind CSS docs, WAI-ARIA Practices for alerts and notes
findings.relevance: CalloutBox variant prop is the only polymorphic pattern in shared_ui; must be exhaustive and accessible

findings.finding: Per operating procedures, vi.mock() factories MUST provide every named runtime export. For shared_ui, the runtime exports will be: CodeBlock, VersionBadge, YouTubeEmbed, CalloutBox. The type exports (CodeBlockProps, etc., CalloutVariant) do NOT need to be in vi.mock() factories since they are erased at runtime. Consumers mocking shared_ui must list all four components. A common pitfall is forgetting one component in the mock factory, causing 'undefined is not a function' errors in consumer tests.
findings.relevance: Directly affects how downstream modules (page_content, step pages) will mock shared_ui in their tests

findings.finding: For a multi-component shared module, the standard pattern is: each component in its own file (e.g., CodeBlock.tsx, VersionBadge.tsx), re-exported from an index.ts barrel file using `export { CodeBlock } from './CodeBlock'` and `export type { CodeBlockProps } from './CodeBlock'`. This keeps files focused while allowing consumers to import from '@/components/shared' or similar. The barrel file IS the contract surface — it must export exactly the types and components listed in the registry.
findings.source: TypeScript module patterns, project naming conventions
findings.relevance: Defines the module boundary and import paths for all consumers of shared_ui

findings.finding: Best practices: (1) Test rendering with required props — verify key text/elements appear, (2) Test each variant for polymorphic components (CalloutBox), (3) Use `screen.getByRole`, `screen.getByText`, `screen.getByTestId` — prefer accessible queries, (4) For CodeBlock, test that the `code` prop renders inside a <pre> or <code> element, (5) For YouTubeEmbed, test that the iframe src is correctly formed, (6) For VersionBadge, test that componentName and version are both rendered. Common pitfall: testing implementation details (class names) instead of behavior/content.
findings.source: @testing-library/react guiding principles, Kent C. Dodds testing best practices
findings.relevance: All four components need contract tests per operating procedures

findings.finding:
The registry defines OptionalString as 'A string value that may be undefined or empty'. In TypeScript this maps to `string | undefined` (i.e., the prop is optional). For CodeBlockProps.description, YouTubeEmbedProps.title — these should be typed as `description?: string` and `title?: string`. Components must handle both undefined and empty string gracefully — render nothing if falsy. A common pitfall is rendering an empty

tag when description is ''.
findings.source: Canonical Type Registry, TypeScript optional property semantics
findings.relevance: Two of four components have optional string props; incorrect handling creates empty DOM nodes

findings.topic: Accessibility for CodeBlock and Pre-formatted Content
findings.finding:
CodeBlock should use semantic HTML: 
...
. The copy button needs an accessible label (aria-label='Copy to clipboard'). After copying, announce success to screen readers via aria-live region or by changing the button's text. The preformatted block should not have role='img' — it's actual text content that should be readable. Consider tabIndex={0} on the code block for keyboard users who want to select text.
findings.source: WAI-ARIA authoring practices, MDN <pre> element docs
findings.relevance: CodeBlock is the most used shared component (every step page has CLI commands); accessibility is critical

recommended_approach:
Define the shared_ui module as a barrel-exported collection of four React components and their associated types, strictly following the canonical type registry:

1. **File Structure**: One file per component (`CodeBlock.tsx`, `VersionBadge.tsx`, `YouTubeEmbed.tsx`, `CalloutBox.tsx`) plus `types.ts` for `CalloutVariant`, and an `index.ts` barrel that re-exports everything.

2. **Type Exports** (via `export type {}`):
   - `CalloutVariant` — string union: `'gotcha' | 'warning' | 'tip'`
   - `CodeBlockProps` — `{ code: string; description?: string }`
   - `VersionBadgeProps` — `{ componentName: string; version: string }`
   - `YouTubeEmbedProps` — `{ url: string; title?: string }`
   - `CalloutBoxProps` — `{ variant: CalloutVariant; text: string }`

3. **Runtime Exports** (named, no defaults):
   - `CodeBlock` — renders `<pre><code>` with copy button using `navigator.clipboard.writeText`
   - `VersionBadge` — inline badge rendering `componentName` + `version`
   - `YouTubeEmbed` — responsive iframe with URL-to-embed conversion, `aspect-video` Tailwind wrapper
   - `CalloutBox` — variant-styled container using a `Record<CalloutVariant, string>` class map

4. **Contract Tests**: One `.test.tsx` file per component using vitest + @testing-library/react. Test: renders correctly with required props, handles optional props being undefined/empty, copy button calls clipboard API (CodeBlock), all three variants render distinct styling (CalloutBox), iframe src is correct (YouTubeEmbed).

5. **Mock Surface Documentation**: Clearly document that consumers mocking this module need exactly four runtime exports: `{ CodeBlock, VersionBadge, YouTubeEmbed, CalloutBox }`.
alternatives_considered: Using TypeScript `enum` keyword for CalloutVariant instead of string union — rejected because string unions are more idiomatic in modern TS, work better with `export type {}`, avoid runtime overhead, and are JSON-serializable without transformation. The registry's 'enum' label maps naturally to a union type.

Single-file approach with all four components in one shared-ui.tsx — rejected because it hurts tree-shaking, makes diffs noisier, and complicates individual component testing. Barrel re-export provides the same single-import ergonomics.

Using a third-party clipboard library (e.g., clipboard.js) instead of native navigator.clipboard — rejected because the native API is well-supported in modern browsers, simpler to mock in tests, and avoids an unnecessary dependency.
Using a YouTube embed library (e.g., react-youtube, lite-youtube-embed) — rejected to minimize dependencies for a simple iframe wrapper. A lightweight URL parser utility is sufficient.

Defining props inline (React.FC<{ code: string }>) without named prop types — rejected because the canonical registry explicitly defines named prop structs that must be exported for cross-module consumption.
risks: YouTube URL parsing edge cases: URLs with timestamps (?t=120), playlist params (?list=...), shorts URLs (/shorts/), and non-standard formats could break embed. Mitigation: implement a focused extractVideoId utility with explicit format handling and tests for each format.

navigator.clipboard.writeText unavailability: In non-secure contexts (HTTP, not HTTPS) or older browsers, the API may be undefined. Mitigation: guard with `if (navigator.clipboard?.writeText)` and provide a fallback or graceful degradation.

Tailwind class purging: If variant-driven class strings are dynamically constructed (e.g., template literals like `bg-${color}-50`), Tailwind's JIT compiler won't detect them. Mitigation: always use complete static class strings in the variant lookup map.

vi.mock() drift: If a new component is added to shared_ui later, all consumer mock factories must be updated. Mitigation: document the mock contract clearly and consider a test helper that validates mock completeness.

Empty string vs undefined for OptionalString props: Components might render empty containers when description='' is passed. Mitigation: use falsy checks (`if (!description)`) rather than strict undefined checks.
compliance_notes: All source files must be .ts or .tsx — no .js, .jsx, or .py files
All public functions must have explicit TypeScript return type annotations
Named exports only — no `export default` anywhere in the module
Type aliases and interfaces must use `export type { }` syntax
CalloutVariant, CodeBlockProps, VersionBadgeProps, YouTubeEmbedProps, CalloutBoxProps must match canonical registry exactly — same names, same fields, same field types
vi.mock() factories for this module must include all four runtime exports: CodeBlock, VersionBadge, YouTubeEmbed, CalloutBox
Every component function must have at least one vitest test
Tests must run without external services (mock clipboard API, no real YouTube fetches)
Import sibling modules using exact exported names — never guess at export names
